naslov: The Attempted Seduction and the Invitation to Sin

segmenti.tekst: نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ الْقَصَصِ بِمَا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ هَٰذَا الْقُرْآنَ وَإِنْ كُنْتَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الْغَافِلِينَ
segmenti.prevod: “We relate to you the best of stories in revealing to you this Qur’an, though before it you were among the unaware.” (Yusuf 12:3)

segmenti.tekst: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ
segmenti.prevod: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and all his companions.

segmenti.tekst: We continue further with the tafsir (exegesis) of Surah Yusuf.

After Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam, was bought by the governor, or chief minister, of Egypt and brought to the palace, he ordered his wife to make his stay pleasant, to treat him well and to give him everything he needed so that he could live with dignity.
The Qur'an further informs us with the words: “And when he reached maturity and full strength, We gave Yusuf the ability to judge justly and We gave him knowledge,” sharpness of mind.
“And just as We granted Yusuf” to be rescued from the well and to be bought by this chief minister of Egypt, because of his good deeds, “so too,” He says, “will We reward all those who do good.”

This is glad tidings for our Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him). Because the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, at that moment was perhaps in the hardest moments of his life. Because at that time the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, had lost his wife and his paternal uncle had passed away.

So the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, was then in his hardest moments. And here Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala (glorified and exalted is He), tells him that, just as Allah rescued Yusuf and rewarded him, Allah will rescue him too from the difficult situation.

As we said: when Yusuf reached maturity… We have often mentioned the hadith in which the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: “Utiya Yusufu shatr al-husn” – he said: Yusuf was given half of all beauty, and the other half of beauty was distributed among other people. So he was very handsome, he was an exceptionally handsome young man.
A young man who lived, of course, with the governor and his wife, who had been ordered to look upon him as her own child.

But she did not look upon him as her own child. She did not look upon him as her own child; rather, she looked at him with other eyes. As the Qur'an tells us: “وَرَاوَدَتْهُ الَّتِي هُوَ فِي بَيْتِهَا عَنْ نَفْسِهِ وَغَلَّقَتِ الْأَبْوَابَ وَقَالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ” – so, it says, one day she invited him to fornication.

She invited him to fornication and locked all the doors in the palace. And she said: “هَيْتَ لَكَ” – that is: “Hayta lak,” meaning: “I have made myself ready for you. I have made myself ready for you.”
In the Arabic language this “al-murawadah” means that she was inviting him in a gentle way, making that act appear attractive to him.
And he answered: “Qala ma'adhallah” – he said: “May Allah protect me, may Allah protect me, I seek refuge with Allah from that to which you invite me. Innahu Rabbi ahsana mathway.”
“Indeed,” he said, “Allah has treated me well and made my stay here pleasant.” So Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, as Yusuf says, has treated me well:

He rescued me from the well, saved me from my brothers, brought me here to the palace and granted me everything. The mufassirun (Qur'an commentators) say – there is also another opinion – that when Yusuf says: “Innahu rabbi” – indeed, he says, this one of mine, the one who bought me, this governor, he says, “has made my stay good and provided me with everything,” and he says: “How could I betray him, how could I betray him?” So Yusuf explained, or justified, this refusal of fornication with the words

that he would not do it because his master had treated him well. The second thing, he says, he says: “Indeed,” he says, “the wrongdoer will not succeed, the wrongdoer will never succeed.” Why? Because he would repay the good done to him with evil. So he says: such a man will not, will not succeed. Also, Yusuf did not want to wrong himself.
And the fourth thing, and the fourth thing, it says: he saw, he saw Allah's signs, or proofs. He saw Allah's signs and proofs.

So he did not want at all, at all to do it. And so Yusuf, alayhis-salam, refused that woman. He refused, he refused fornication. And you know, dear brothers, that hadith, you have surely heard it, that seven will be in the shade of the Throne on the Day of Judgment, when people will be drowning in their sweat, that seven will be in the shade of Allah's Throne on the Day of Judgment.

Among them, he said: “wa rajulun da'athu imra'atun dhatu mansibin wa jamalin fa qala: inni akhafullah” – he said: a man whom a woman of status and beauty invites to fornication, and he says: “I fear Allah,” he says, “I fear Allah, I will not do it, I will not do it.” The Qur'an further informs us, it says: “Wa laqad hammat bihi” – and, it says, she desired him.
She wanted to commit fornication with him. “وَهَمَّ بِهَا” – and he would have desired her – “لَوْلَا أَنْ رَأَى بُرْهَانَ رَبِّهِ” – had he not seen the proof of his Lord.

In the Arabic language this “لَوْلَا” is called “harf al-imtina'”, a particle meaning that something could not happen, or that it is impossible for something to happen, because a certain condition was not fulfilled.

A certain condition was not fulfilled, so Yusuf could not in any way have desired her. Why? Because he had seen Allah's signs: from the dream he dreamt as a child, to the angel who came to him in the well.

Some say that he saw, it is said, the image of his father at that moment. Some mufassirun say that he saw an angel. Some say that at that moment he saw written on the wall: “wa la taqrabu az-zina” – and, it says, do not come near fornication.

So, so Yusuf withdrew. He did not want to commit fornication and it did not interest him. And here a person, when reading these verses, especially someone who does not understand Arabic, must by no means think that Yusuf desired her.

That is, in Arabic it means that it could never happen that he would desire her. Why? Because he was one of Allah's chosen servants. He was a prophet. That could not happen to him. Not at all. Other mufassirun, however, say: “wa laqad hammat bihi” – they say: she wanted, it is said, to strike him, to teach him a lesson:

“How dare you refuse me? Who are you to refuse me? I am the first lady of Egypt, and you are a nobody. Where do you get the right to refuse me?” And, it is said, he wanted to strike her at that moment.

He wanted to strike her at that moment, and Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, sent him certain signs, and he held back, because it would have cost him a great deal. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: “Kadhalika li nasrifa 'anhu as-su'a” –

He says: that is what We did, that is, We gave him those signs, in order to turn away from him what is evil, to turn away from him betrayal, to turn away from him “al-fahsha'”, that abominable act of fornication.
“Innahu min 'ibadina al-mukhlasin” – He says: indeed, He says, he is among Our sincere, chosen servants. So Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam, is among Allah's sincere, chosen servants.

When Yusuf saw that nothing worked with this woman, neither advice nor anything else, he set off, set off toward the door to get out. And here, here we stop, and tomorrow, in sha Allah, in sha Allahu ta'ala, we will continue. May Allah grant you every good. As-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.
